newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes lower, faces fresh pressure.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes lower, faces fresh pressure.

text.p: Precious metals prices are likely to come under pressure later on Monday and for the rest of the week following weakness in silver and platinum last Friday, dealers said.
"Gold held up well but it couldn't take the extra pressure of selling in silver and platinum," one dealer said.
It was fixed at $343.35 per ounce, down from $344.50 on Friday, having edged lower late in New York and in the Far East markets earlier today.
The market was rocked late last week when Germany, hitherto a staunch suppporter of gold as a reserve asset, announced it would revalue the Bundesbank's gold reserves closer to market value.
Comment from leading German financial officials linked the decision to plugging an unexpected gap of about 18 billion marks in the 1997 budget.
"Regardless of the (German) central bank stance, it looks as though some people have wakened up to the change in sentiment," one dealer said of the weaker price.
"The central bank move puts gold's longer-term prospects in doubt," he added.
Few fireworks were expected during morning trading as most of Europe was closed for a holiday and London business was cautious ahead of the New York opening.
Gold faced a critical level at $342.00-$343.00 which, according to technical evidence, should provide a good level of buying support, dealers said.
"But it has the distinct potential to go a lot lower if $342 is broken,"a dealer warned, adding that on the upside $345.00 should offer stiff resistance.
Silver final broke down on Friday afternoon, having been almost motionless for two days after jumping last Wednesday to $4.8735, its highest fixing since early April.
"The funds were selling almost as soon as New York opened and that was it," a dealer said.
Silver ended down 15 cents at $4.70/$4.72 on Friday and was a cent lower on Monday morning.
Some dealers were looking for silver to turn lower again later in the week.
Some of the steam had come out of platinum as well by Monday with prices at $388.25/$389.25 -- down $2.50 from Friday and over $7.00 down since last Wednesday's peak.
